chunks.content: # Designer’s CLO Journey | Basic Skirt 3D Revision Tutorial This document provides a detailed guide on modifying basic skirt patterns using CLO 3D software, focusing on pattern editing, panel manipulation, fold creation, fabric application, and accessory integration. It covers techniques such as pattern extension, panel merging, fold tool usage, stitching, invisible zippers, and advanced detailing like butterfly knots and D-rings. --- ## Introduction to Basic Skirt Modification in CLO This section introduces the process of transforming a basic half-body dress/skirt pattern into designed garment groups using CLO 3D. It includes importing patterns, using reference images, and basic fabric application. - Start with a basic half-body dress/skirt pattern. - Import a reference image alongside the pattern to guide design and modifications. - Apply a single piece of fabric to the pattern before adjustments. - Use the shrink-to-fit function to align fabric and pattern. - Create reverse or hidden versions of pattern files if needed. - Recognize that basic patterns include shortcuts and divisions that may require extension or merging. --- ## Pattern Division and Extension Techniques This section explains how to divide and extend skirt patterns to modify length and shape, using CLO's editing tools. - Use the **Edit Pattern Tool** to lengthen panels by entering specific values (e.g., extend skirt by 200 mm). - Draw internal design lines using the **Internal Line Tool** on 2D boards for accurate pattern shapes. - Align points and lines precisely with right-click alignment tools. - Utilize the **Smooth Curve Tool** to adjust arcs and create rounded shapes. - Panels linked together only require adjustments on one side for symmetrical changes. - Use **Cut and Sew Tool** to segment panels along drawn internal lines. - Adjust curves and lines simultaneously on top and bottom edges for balanced shapes. - 3D window editing tools can refine noise and curve smoothness on panels. --- ## Panel Merging and Extension for Design Effects This section covers merging side panels and extending them to create styles such as lantern or lotus leaf shapes. - Use the **Edit Panel Tool** to select adjacent panels, then right-click and select **Merge** to combine into a whole panel. - Apply the **Extension Panel Tool** to stretch panels in desired directions (top, bottom, or both). - Enter specific extension distances to control the amount of expansion (positive values extend, negative values shrink). - Example effects: - Extending line 1 length for lantern-style panels. - Extending line 2 length for lotus leaf-style panels. - After extension, simulate in the 3D window to observe panel interaction and overlap. - Adjust extension values iteratively to achieve the desired size and shape. --- ## Adding Details: Fluttering Waist and Fabric Effects This section details creating fluttering effects on the waist and applying realistic fabric textures. - Create an internal line on the panel edge to define fluttering areas. - Adjust waist height for smooth transition effects. - Use RPM (Rotation, Position, and Magnitude) settings to shape the fluttering internal lines.
